title: Kummer etale sharp-chart refinement with a prescribed base chart
statement:
Let $f:(X,M_X)\to(Y,M_Y)$ be a Kummer etale morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-per-kummer-log-morphism, def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Let $\bar x$ be a geometric point of $X$ and put $\bar y=f(\bar x)$. Suppose a chart $a:P\to M_Y$ is given on $Y$, where $P$ is sharp fs (zero is its only unit) and its map to $\overline M_{Y,\bar y}$ is an isomorphism. There exist pointed etale neighbourhoods $U\to Y$ of $\bar y$ and $W\to X\times_YU$ of the induced point, a sharp fs monoid $Q$ with chart $b:Q\to M_W$ inducing $Q\simeq\overline M_{X,\bar x}$, and an injective homomorphism $h:P\to Q$ such that every $q\in Q$ has a positive multiple in $h(P)$. They satisfy $b\circ h=f_W^\flat(a|_U)$. The map $h^{\rm gp}$ is injective with finite cokernel annihilated by an integer $n>0$ invertible on $U$, and the scheme comparison
$$W\longrightarrow U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$$
is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product]. Monoid rings and chart comparison have the meaning of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. No finiteness of $f$, strict locality, log regularity, reducedness or flatness of the underlying morphism is assumed.

source.place: VI 2.2, p.72, etale-local standard-cover assertion (citing Stix 2002, 3.1.4); VI 3.7(a), p.75, sharp stalk sections and chart spreading. The prescribed sharp-base-chart refinement is an agent formulation of this local chart input; direct Stix source WANTED in report.

proof.text: First show that the relative logarithmic differential sheaf $\omega_f$ is zero. The log-etale hypothesis implies log smoothness by [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change]. By [lem-per-fs-log-infinitesimal-criterion], the underlying map is locally of finite presentation and every strict square-zero test square of fine log schemes has exactly one global log lift. In particular lifts exist etale locally. These are the hypotheses of [lem-per-infinitesimal-log-differential-calculus], whose final clause gives $\omega_f=0$. The required stability of the existence hypothesis under compatible etale restriction follows by restricting the log-etale chart data and applying the same infinitesimal criterion. Thus the differential basis at $\bar x$ is the empty basis.

source.place: X proof of Proposition 1.2, pp.136--138; XVI proof of Proposition 3.6.3, p.252, empty differential basis for a log-etale map.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $E=M_{X,\bar x}^{\rm gp}$, $D=A^\times\subset E$, and $R=\overline M_{X,\bar x}$. Apply [lem-per-very-tame-equivariant-sharp-chart] with the trivial group: its order is $1$, and its action on $R$ is trivial. In particular $R$ is sharp fs. Applying [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] with the unit face $\{0\}$ to $P$ and $R$ gives finite free groups $L=P^{\rm gp}$ and $R^{\rm gp}=E/D$. Let $\varphi:L\to E$ be pullback of the given chart germ. Apply [lem-per-log-smooth-differential-generators] to $f$ and this prescribed $P$-chart, whose group is torsion-free. Since $\omega_{f,\bar x}=0$, its basis has length zero. The lemma supplies an integer $n\ge1$ invertible in $A$, $n$-divisibility of $D$, and a finite cokernel of $L\to E/D$ killed by $n$. The map $P\to R$ here is precisely the characteristic map using the given identification $P\simeq\overline M_{Y,\bar y}$.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), p.75, sharp characteristic and its free group; XVI proof of Proposition 3.6.3, p.252, characteristic cokernel and divisible strict-local units.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-divisible-unit-lattice-extension] to $(L,E,D,\varphi,n)$. The finite-free source, torsion-free quotient, divisible units and finite cokernel hypotheses were verified in step 2. Obtain a finite free group $G$, an injection $i:L\hookrightarrow G$ and a lift $s:G\to E$ with $si=\varphi$, such that $G/i(L)$ is killed by $n^k$ for some $k\ge0$ and $\rho:G\to E/D=R^{\rm gp}$ induced by $s$ is surjective. This uses the prescribed chart map $\varphi$, so it does not replace that chart by an unrelated one.

source.place: XVI Lemma 3.6.4, pp.252--253, applied with zero relative differential rank.

proof.text: The map $\rho$ is also injective. If $\rho(g)=0$, write $n^kg=i(p)$ for $p\in L$. Then the characteristic group map sends $p$ to zero. Its monoid map $P\to R$ is injective by Kummerness [def-per-kummer-log-morphism], so its group map is injective: equality of differences reduces to equality of sums in the integral monoids. Hence $p=0$, and torsion-freeness of $G$ gives $g=0$. Define $Q=s^{-1}(M_{X,\bar x})\subset G$. An element $e\in E$ belongs to $M_{X,\bar x}$ exactly when its image in $R^{\rm gp}$ belongs to $R$: in the reverse direction choose a log element with that characteristic and subtract the remaining unit. This uses the integral log monoid and its quotient by units [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Consequently $Q=\rho^{-1}(R)$, and $\rho$ identifies $Q$ with $R$. In particular $Q$ is sharp fs and generates $G$.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; XVI proof of Proposition 3.6.3, p.252, inverse-image monoid. Agent argument: Kummer injectivity makes the auxiliary lattice map an isomorphism.

proof.text: The homomorphism $h:P\to Q$ is $p\mapsto i(p)$: it lands in $Q$ since $si(p)=f^\flat(a(p))$. It is injective. For $q\in Q$, characteristic Kummerness [def-per-kummer-log-morphism] supplies $d>0$ and $p\in P$ with $d\rho(q)=\rho i(p)$. Since $\rho$ is injective, $dq=i(p)=h(p)$. The group map is $i:L\to G$ under $Q^{\rm gp}=G$, so its cokernel is killed by $n^k$. It is finite: for a finite basis of $G$, reduce each coefficient modulo $n^k$ to obtain finitely many representatives of $G/i(L)$. When $n^k=1$ the quotient is zero.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72, Kummer maps; XVI Lemma 3.6.4, pp.252--253, finite-exponent auxiliary lattice quotient. Elementary consequences of steps 3--4.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-kato-lattice-chart-realization] with base monoid $P$ (called $Q$ in that lemma), $r=0$, the empty differential basis, and the $G,i,s,n$ of steps 2--3. All its hypotheses hold: $f$ is log smooth, $P^{\rm gp}$ is torsion-free, $n$ is invertible in $A$, $si=\varphi$, $G/i(L)$ is killed by a power of $n$, and $G\to E/D$ is surjective. Its prescribed inverse-image monoid is exactly our $Q$. It yields a pointed etale neighbourhood $W_0\to X$ and a chart $b_0:Q\to M_{W_0}$ with germ $s|_Q$, compatible with the given $P$-chart through $h$, and an etale comparison $W_0\to Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$. The induced characteristic map of this chart is $\rho|_Q:Q\simeq R$ by step 4. Compatibility means the equality of log sections $b_0h=f_{W_0}^\flat a$, not merely equality of their characteristic classes.

source.place: XVI proof of Proposition 3.6.3, p.252, last paragraph: prescribed inverse-image monoid, chart spreading and etale comparison.

proof.text: It remains to put the annihilator on the base. The geometric local ring map $\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}\to A$ is local; if $n$ were in the maximal ideal downstairs, its image would be in the maximal ideal of $A$. Thus $n$ is invertible at $\bar y$. Represent its inverse by a section near $\bar y$ and restrict until its product with $n$ is $1$. This gives an open neighbourhood $U\subset Y$ where $n$, hence $N=n^k>0$, is invertible. The open immersion $U\to Y$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Put $W=W_0\times_YU$. The map $W\to X\times_YU$ is the base change of $W_0\to X$, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The comparison for $W\to U$ is the base change of the comparison in step 6 and is etale by the same lemma. Restrict $b_0$ and $a$ to obtain $b$ and $a|_U$. Their equality remains $bh=f_W^\flat(a|_U)$, and their germs at the induced geometric points are unchanged by these open restrictions. Steps 4--5 give sharpness, the characteristic isomorphism, Kummerness, injectivity of the group map, and its finite cokernel annihilated by $N$. Rename $N$ as the statement's integer. This proves all the required clauses.

source.place: VI 2.2, p.72, invertible annihilator on the base; restriction of the XVI 3.6.3 chart. Stacks Tags 02GO and 02GT for etale base change and open immersions.

proof_origin.place: VI 2.2 and 3.7(a), pp.72,75; X proof of Proposition 1.2, pp.136--138; XVI Proposition 3.6.3 and Lemma 3.6.4, pp.252--253. Assembly with the Kummer-injective lattice argument in steps 4--5 written by Q69.

Step-by-step checks: (1) log etale => log smooth, the infinitesimal criterion gives unique global lifts, so omega_f=0 and r=0. (2) The very-tame lemma with the trivial group gives sharp fs characteristic; the generators lemma with the prescribed P-chart gives n invertible, n-divisible units and a finite cokernel killed by n. (3) The lattice extension gives G, i, s and rho surjective. (4) An injective map of integral monoids is injective on groups, so Kummer injectivity plus torsion-free G makes rho an isomorphism, and Q=s^{-1}(M)=rho^{-1}(R) is sharp fs. (5) h=i|_P is Kummer with finite cokernel killed by n^k. (6) Kato lattice realization with r=0: all hypotheses checked; it keeps the prescribed base chart and gives an etale comparison. (7) A local ring map shows n is invertible on an open U; base changes are etale (02GO). Small cases checked: trivial log structures, the d-root chart, empty X.
